_about.what: Every figure on the card-counting results page, with its interval and its source.
_about.unit: Expected value in percent of the minimum bet (one unit) per round dealt, unless a figure's key says otherwise. Keys beginning perbet are per amount bet: the per-round figure divided by the average bet of the same schedule (keys beginning avgbet).
_about.keys: SCOPE.PEN.SPREAD.ROW. SCOPE: bet = the count used for bets and insurance only, the chart for play; fd = also for the first decision on the two cards dealt; full = for every decision in the round; fdw and fullw = the same with wonging. PEN = where the cut card sits, in percent of the shoe. SPREAD = s1 for flat bets, sN for the same bet schedule from 1 to N units. ROW = the count, named in the names block.
_about.plays: Every play is taken from index tables fitted for this game from the data, not from the authors' published index lists.
_about.schedule: The same bet schedule for every count: the same bet sizes, handed out in the order of each count's own estimate of the advantage.
_about.side_counts: A row whose id ends in _ace keeps a side count of aces; the tables block says where each row's rule comes from.
_about.intervals: se is the bootstrap standard error over resampled shoes; ci is the 95% interval. Full-play intervals are widened as FULL_INDEX_PLAYS.md section 4 says (widen gives the ratio).
_about.figures: Each figure: value, se, ci, fmt (how the page prints it), src (the artifact it was read from), at (where in that artifact; the key itself when left out), commit (the commit that made the artifact), file (main, the main state file, when left out; search, the second file the searched count was chosen on). A figure that is also a grid cell is given once, in the grid.
_about.grid: The figures the page's controls switch among, one row per count: _layout names the four numbers of a cell; _sources gives each row and scope's input (an index into inputs) and whether its intervals were widened. A cell's key is SCOPE.PEN.SPREAD.ROW and its at is that key.

same.words: A computer search for the best count of this kind, run on a separate set of 60,000 shoes and then scored once here, found one that beats every published count I tested: [ROW] scores [EV]% of a unit a round at 80% penetration with a 1-8 spread, [GAIN] more than the best published row, [BEST], and every published count by at least [LOWER] (the smallest lower end of the 95% intervals). The gain is small next to the room left above it: perfect knowledge of the cards left would earn [PERFECT]. The count's tags are not meant for a person to keep; they show how much better a count of ten numbers can do at this game, not a system to play.

flat.words: Flat-betting, the searched count F1 flat beats every published count I tested, by at least [LOWER].

evidence.check: ExactRound against BruteForceRound, two programs written apart from ROUND_CONTRACT.md
evidence.recorded: 3,000 random cases on shoes of 14 to 24 cards: 11,420 rounds valued by both, the worst gap 1.3e-15, and 1,930 left out as too big for the brute force; 1,500 cases on shoes of 1 to 13 cards; 600 splits on shoes of 30 to 50 cards; a longer run on another seed, 114,633 rounds valued by both, the worst gap 2.0e-15
evidence.catches: the exact engine's logic, on the shoes tested
evidence.misses: a rule the contract itself states wrongly; rounds too big for the brute force

evidence.check: Six bugs planted in ExactRound after its tests were written
evidence.recorded: each made the suite fail; the last, a split ace hit when the rules say it may not be, only because the run ran out of memory, not by a failed assertion
evidence.catches: how often the tests catch a bug in the engine
evidence.misses: bugs of other kinds than those planted

evidence.check: Standing on 16 to 20 against the infinite deck's value
evidence.recorded: the gap shrinks as one over the number of decks, and is under 1e-4 at 512 decks
evidence.catches: errors that grow with the size of the shoe
evidence.misses: errors the infinite deck's value shares

evidence.check: The chart (basic strategy) against the exact engine
evidence.recorded: the 4-8 deck chart for a dealer who hits soft 17: its first move is the exact engine's best for all 540 two-card hands against every up-card off the top of an eight-deck shoe under Montreal's rules
evidence.catches: a wrong cell of the chart every count starts from
evidence.misses: the chart's play after the first move

evidence.check: The player tree against the stored values, on the whole main file
evidence.recorded: on all 60,743 states, 320,392,174 Hit values and 32,789,360 Stand values set beside the stored ones, the largest difference 7.8e-16
evidence.catches: a tree that values a hand otherwise than the stored states

evidence.check: Bugs planted in the scorer by its reviewers
evidence.recorded: two reviewers planted 24 and 38 bugs in scratch copies of the scorer and the report
evidence.catches: how often the tests catch a bug in the scorer
evidence.misses: bugs of other kinds than those planted

evidence.check: The scorer's planted bugs that passed every test
evidence.recorded: planted again after a first round of new tests, eight in the scorer and one in the report still passed every test, and new tests were written for them
evidence.catches: the gaps a first round of tests left
evidence.misses: gaps no reviewer planted a bug in

evidence.check: A recheck of the scorer review's findings, each planted bug put back into the final code
evidence.recorded: 52 of 57 findings fixed, and five still open, none of them changing a number

evidence.check: Bugs a review planted in SplitValues
evidence.recorded: four passed every test; three new SplitValuesTest cases now hold the code where they did not
evidence.catches: a split valued from the wrong print or store

evidence.check: Bugs the play's two walks share
evidence.recorded: planted by a review, they passed every test, since the only test of the gaps set one walk beside the other; each gap is now held to the change flipping one cell makes
evidence.catches: a gap both walks get wrong

evidence.check: The bound a later cell of full play is charged
evidence.recorded: a planted bug charging max(0, 2 SE - |gain|) for max(0, 2 SE - gain) passed every test; LaterCallTest now fails on it
evidence.catches: a later cell charged too little

evidence.check: One look at the main file
evidence.recorded: the search tools refuse a main-seed state file, each before it writes anything; the runs that score it name the registration's blob and add one ledger line a look
evidence.catches: a search that reads the main file, or a look at it the ledger does not record
evidence.misses: guards in code the author controls

evidence.check: The bootstrap's SE against the spread of disjoint sub-runs
evidence.recorded: for an EV it is close, 0.115% against 0.114% for Hi-Lo; for Red Seven's difference from Hi-Lo it is under the spread, 0.031% against 0.045%; for Omega II's, about three to four times the spread
evidence.catches: an interval too narrow for the spread it stands for
